claim: City of Traverse Regional WWTP serves 50,000 residents and local industries with 8.5-mgd capacity.
Traverse City’s MBR upgrade increased peak flow capacity to 17-mgd and Jacobs manages five satellite projects, including 0.069-mgd and 0.132-mgd facilities.
Traverse City operates nine lift stations; Front St. Lift Station can deliver over 1-mgd and has capacity to deliver 8.7-mgd.
Traverse City’s two upgrades included a $1.5 million 1999 BNR improvement and a $31 million 2004 MBR upgrade; the plant can handle 17-mgd peak flow.
Traverse City received over $1.6 million in 2023 for rooftop solar and battery storage producing 10% of annual energy usage.
Traverse City staff reduced electrical consumption by over 30% after MBR optimization.
Spokane County Regional Water Reclamation Facility is 8.5-mgd, expandable to 24-mgd, and reduces phosphorus below 50 PPB.
Spokane SCRWRF was built on a 20-acre site and selected Jacobs in 2008 after planning that began in 1999.
Spokane MBR and nutrient-removal systems achieve 50 ppb phosphorus and 0.25 mg/L ammonia.
Spokane started up approximately seven months ahead of schedule; NPDES permit was received November 30, 2011 and discharge began December 1, 2011.

claim: Clovis is a 3.1-mgd, $37-million reuse facility that saved the City more than $100,000 through value engineering.
